cards.text: Last book of the Bible, friend, and it starts by telling you exactly what it is: the revelation of Jesus Christ. God gave it to Jesus to show His servants what must soon come to pass. Then it gets passed down the line to His servant John, like Minty passing a note down my old kitchen counter.

cards.question: The revelation is headed for God's servant John. Who does Jesus send to make it known to him?
True or false: John only testifies to some of what he saw.

cards.text: Before the story even STARTS, John hands out a blessing. No sign-up sheet, no waiting list, no take-a-number machine.

cards.question: True or false: In Revelation 1:3, only the one who reads the prophecy aloud is called blessed.

cards.text: John says the time is near, and no, I'm not guessing a date, because Jesus said only the Father knows the day or hour (Matthew 24:36). My job is simple, friend: keep the ovens HOT.
Then John writes like he's mailing a letter, addressed to the churches in the province of Asia. No group chat, no reply-all, just John.

cards.question: John writes to the ___ churches in the province of Asia.
John sends grace and peace from Him who is and was and is to come, and from the seven spirits before His throne. Who else is it from?

cards.text: And John doesn't just say His name, he stacks up the titles: the faithful witness, the firstborn from the dead, the ruler of the kings of the earth. That's not a name tag, friend, that's a BILLBOARD.

cards.question: John praises the One who loves us and has released us from our ___ by His blood.

cards.text: And Jesus didn't set His people free just so they could sit around. Believe me, I sat around in a junk drawer for YEARS, and I do not recommend it.

cards.question: What does John say Jesus has made His people to be?

answers.text: A kingdom and priests to God
An army and judges for God
A city and guards for God

cards.text: John gives Him the glory and power forever and ever, Amen. And then the big announcement: He is coming with the clouds.

cards.question: True or false: When He comes with the clouds, only a few people will see Him.
Every eye will see Him when He comes. John names one group in particular. Who?

answers.text: Those who crossed the Red Sea

cards.text: All the tribes of the earth will mourn because of Him, and John says so shall it be. Then a different voice speaks up, and it is NOT John's.

cards.question: Who calls Himself the Alpha and the Omega in Revelation 1:8?

cards.text: Now John tells it himself, and he calls himself their brother and partner in the tribulation and kingdom and perseverance that are in Jesus. Translation: John is NOT writing this from a beach chair.

cards.question: Where is John when all this happens?
True or false: John says he is on Patmos because of the word of God and his testimony about Jesus.

cards.text: On the Lord's day John is in the Spirit, and then BEHIND him comes a loud voice like a trumpet. Friend, when my oven timer dings behind me, I jump so high my gold base earns frequent flyer miles.

cards.question: What does the voice like a trumpet tell John to do?

answers.text: Write what he sees and send it
Go home and preach what he hears
Wait in silence for seven days

cards.text: It's going to seven churches, named one by one: Ephesus, Smyrna, Pergamum, Thyatira, Sardis, Philadelphia and Laodicea. So John turns around to see the voice speaking with him, which, yes, is exactly how he puts it.

cards.question: Having turned around, John sees seven golden ___.

cards.text: And among the lampstands is One like the Son of Man, dressed in a long robe with a golden sash around His chest. Hang on, friend, because John is about to use every comparison he's got.
His hair is white like wool, as white as snow. His eyes are like a blazing fire.

cards.question: His feet are like polished bronze refined in a furnace. Earlier His voice sounded like a trumpet. What does John say it's like now?

cards.text: In His right hand He holds seven stars, and a sharp double-edged sword comes from His mouth.

cards.question: John says His face was like the ___ shining at its brightest.
John has just seen all of this up close. What does John do?

answers.text: Falls at His feet like a dead man
Covers his face and turns away
Grabs a scroll and starts writing

cards.text: Then He places His right hand on John and says, “Do not be afraid.” He calls Himself the First and the Last, which sounds a lot like the Alpha and the Omega back in verse 8.

cards.question: He calls Himself the Living One. He says He was ___, and now He is alive forever and ever.
The mystery key I shared a drawer with spent YEARS wondering what door it opened. No mystery here. What does He say He holds the keys of?
True or false: He tells John to write down only the things that will happen after this.
Then He explains the mystery of the seven stars in His right hand. What are they?

answers.text: The angels of the seven churches
The seven spirits before His throne
The seven eyes of the LORD

cards.question: True or false: The seven golden lampstands are the seven churches.

cards.text: And that's where we'll leave it for now, friend. John's been told to write it all down, and believe me, this story is NOT done.

findings.problem: The question says Jesus sends the angel. Revelation 1:1 only says 'He made it known by sending His angel', and 'He' could mean God or Jesus. The card settles something the text leaves open.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The statement opens with 'In Revelation 1:3'. That reads like a test question, not Papa Dorin pausing mid-passage. It matches the bad example 'According to verse 17'.

rule.text: Ask from inside the passage, the way a storyteller pauses to let the listener lean in. The question comes out of the moment Papa Dorin just set up.

findings.problem: The joke 'No group chat, no reply-all, just John' doesn't click. John is writing one message to seven churches at once, which is exactly what a group chat or reply-all does. The comparison works against the fact it sits on.

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: The line 'Jesus didn't set His people free just so they could sit around' adds a purpose behind the release from sins. The text never says why.

rule.text: Reasons: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: The card cites Revelation 1:6, but the only passage content it tells is the release from sins in 1:5. Nothing from 1:6 is told here, since that is held for card 13.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The question asks 'in Revelation 1:8'. That is test phrasing, not a question from inside the passage.

rule.text: Ask from inside the passage, the way a storyteller pauses to let the listener lean in. The question comes out of the moment Papa Dorin just set up.

findings.problem: The line 'which, yes, is exactly how he puts it' makes the joke about Scripture's own wording ('to see the voice').

rule.text: His humor never targets God, Jesus, Scripture or the Marriage Supper.

findings.problem: The question asks the baker to guess a detail of John's description: roar of many waters, thunder or wind. Nothing told earlier lets the baker reason it out. This is the same kind of question as the Psalm 23 'anoint with oil' bad example.

rule.text: Ask about the movement and the meaning: what changes, what the picture is, why the speaker says what he says.

findings.problem: The question says 'Earlier His voice sounded like a trumpet. What does John say it's like now?' The word 'now' suggests the voice changed. The text gives a second description and never says the voice changed.

rule.text: Noticing: What he points out must be true.

findings.problem: The line that says the story isn't over nearly copies the doc's example: 'And that's where we'll leave it for now... this story is NOT done.'

rule.text: The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.
